title: Choosing the right cage
steps: Choose a wide enclosure that allows short flights and wing stretching.
Check bar spacing suits the species and fit secure latches.
caution: Avoid round cages and sharp or rusty bars.

title: Positioning the cage
steps: Place the cage in a bright social room away from draughts and cooking fumes.
Provide a quiet area for undisturbed night-time rest.
caution: Keep out of direct midday sun and away from radiators.

title: Natural wood perches
steps: Offer clean bird-safe branches of varying diameters and textures.
Place perches so droppings do not fall into food and water.
caution: Avoid sandpaper perch covers that irritate feet.

title: Cage floor and liners
steps: Use plain paper liners to observe droppings and replace when soiled.
Keep the base dry and inspect for food waste.
caution: Avoid scented or dusty substrates.

title: Safe food and water bowls
steps: Wash bowls daily and provide fresh drinking water.
Position bowls where they will not be contaminated by droppings.
caution: Never rely on a blocked or dirty water dispenser.

title: Daily spot cleaning
steps: Remove droppings, wet paper and spoiled fresh food.
Wipe affected surfaces with bird-safe products and rinse well.
caution: Move birds away from cleaning sprays and fumes.

title: Deep cleaning the enclosure
steps: Transfer the bird safely to a secure temporary space.
Wash cage parts with appropriate bird-safe cleaner, rinse and dry fully.
caution: Avoid bleach fumes and never mix cleaning chemicals.

title: Introducing a new bird
steps: Set up a separate quarantine space and arrange an avian-vet check.
Introduce birds gradually with supervised contact after veterinary guidance.
caution: Do not put unfamiliar birds directly together.

title: Understanding flock companionship
steps: Offer daily interaction and species-appropriate social contact.
Consider a compatible companion where housing and welfare allow.
caution: A mirror is not a substitute for appropriate social care.

title: Recognising stress signals
steps: Notice repeated escape attempts, freezing, frantic movement or sudden quietness.
Reduce disturbance and identify changes in the environment.
caution: Persistent distress warrants advice from an avian vet.

title: Reading budgie body language
steps: Observe relaxed posture, gentle chirping and comfortable preening.
Watch for fluffed posture combined with inactivity or reduced appetite.
caution: Birds often conceal illness; unusual behaviour matters.

title: Gentle step-up training
steps: Offer a perch or finger at chest height and reward voluntary stepping.
Keep sessions short and stop before the bird becomes fearful.
caution: Never grab or force a frightened bird to step up.

title: Positive reinforcement
steps: Reward desired behaviours promptly with praise or a small suitable treat.
Practise one simple skill at a time in a calm place.
caution: Avoid punishment, shouting or spraying water as discipline.

title: Safe out-of-cage flying
steps: Close doors and windows and cover mirrors and large panes.
Turn off fans and remove other pets before supervised flight.
caution: Never allow free flight in a kitchen during cooking.

title: Bird-safe toys
steps: Provide shredding toys, swings and appropriate foraging materials.
Rotate toys and check them for damage and entanglement hazards.
caution: Remove frayed ropes, small loose parts and unsafe metals.

title: Foraging for food
steps: Hide a little of the normal daily food allowance in safe paper foraging toys.
Start with easy puzzles and increase difficulty gradually.
caution: Do not restrict access to essential food.

title: Managing boredom
steps: Offer varied perches, safe toys and predictable social time.
Watch which activities the bird chooses voluntarily.
caution: Sudden feather damage needs veterinary assessment.

title: Bathing and misting
steps: Offer a shallow bath of clean lukewarm water or a gentle mist if welcomed.
Let feathers dry naturally in a warm, draught-free room.
caution: Never use shampoo or force a bird into water.

title: Normal preening
steps: Allow time for the bird to align feathers with its beak.
Notice changes such as excessive scratching or bald patches.
caution: Persistent feather loss or self-plucking requires an avian vet.

title: Nail care
steps: Check whether nails snag on fabric or affect perching.
Ask an avian vet to demonstrate safe trimming if needed.
caution: Cutting too far can cause serious bleeding.

title: Beak health
steps: Provide safe chewing and foraging opportunities.
Observe whether the beak closes normally and food is handled comfortably.
caution: Do not trim a beak yourself; overgrowth needs veterinary assessment.

title: Balanced budgie diet
steps: Provide a balanced species-appropriate diet developed with avian-vet guidance.
Introduce suitable vegetables gradually alongside the main diet.
caution: A seed-only diet can cause nutritional problems.

title: Safe leafy greens
steps: Offer washed bird-safe greens in small manageable pieces.
Remove uneaten fresh food before it spoils.
caution: Check plant identification and avoid pesticide residues.

title: Introducing new vegetables
steps: Offer tiny portions repeatedly without forcing the bird.
Present vegetables chopped, clipped or alongside familiar food.
caution: Never starve a bird to force a diet change.

title: Treats and millet
steps: Use small millet portions as occasional training rewards.
Count treats as part of the bird's total food intake.
caution: Excess treats can unbalance the diet.

title: Foods to avoid
steps: Keep avocado, chocolate, caffeine and alcohol away from birds.
Prevent access to salty, sugary and heavily seasoned human food.
caution: Suspected ingestion of toxins requires urgent avian-vet advice.

title: Fresh water routines
steps: Refresh drinking water at least daily and more often if contaminated.
Monitor whether the bird drinks normally.
caution: Sudden drinking changes can indicate illness.

title: Monitoring body condition
steps: Weigh the bird on a gram scale at a consistent time if trained to tolerate it.
Record trends and observe appetite and activity.
caution: Unexpected weight loss needs prompt avian-vet assessment.

title: Checking droppings
steps: Observe changes in the appearance and frequency of droppings on paper liners.
Note any dietary changes that could affect colour.
caution: Persistent changes, straining or blood need veterinary advice.

title: Early signs of illness
steps: Watch for lethargy, reduced appetite, unusual fluffed posture or sitting low.
Keep the bird warm and calm while contacting an avian vet.
caution: Birds can deteriorate quickly; do not wait for severe symptoms.

title: Breathing difficulties
steps: Look for open-mouth breathing, pronounced tail bobbing or wheezing.
Reduce stress and arrange emergency avian veterinary care.
caution: Never attempt home respiratory treatments or delay help.

title: Injuries and bleeding
steps: Keep the bird secure and minimise handling after an injury.
Contact an avian vet immediately for bleeding, falls or suspected fractures.
caution: Small birds can lose dangerous amounts of blood quickly.

title: Annual avian health checks
steps: Arrange routine examinations with an avian-experienced vet.
Bring notes on diet, behaviour and weight trends.
caution: A general dog-and-cat clinic may not have bird-specific expertise.

title: Safe transport to the vet
steps: Use a secure ventilated travel carrier with a stable perch or padded floor.
Keep the carrier quiet and protected from temperature extremes.
caution: Never transport a bird loose in a vehicle.

title: Teflon and non-stick fumes
steps: Keep birds away from kitchens and overheated non-stick cookware.
Choose safer cooking practices and ensure good ventilation.
caution: Overheated PTFE fumes can be rapidly fatal to birds.

title: Aerosols and fragrances
steps: Avoid air fresheners, scented candles, essential-oil diffusers and aerosol sprays near birds.
Use fresh air and bird-safe cleaning methods.
caution: Bird respiratory systems are highly sensitive to airborne irritants.

title: Open windows and doors
steps: Check that windows and doors are secured before opening the cage.
Use properly fitted screens and supervise all flight time.
caution: Even tame birds can escape unexpectedly.

title: Ceiling fans and mirrors
steps: Turn off ceiling fans and cover hazardous reflective surfaces before flight.
Walk through the room to identify collision risks.
caution: Window strikes can cause serious injury.

title: Houseplants and toxic materials
steps: Check every houseplant against reliable bird-safety guidance.
Keep unknown plants, lead, zinc and peeling paint out of reach.
caution: Chewing toxic items can cause poisoning.

title: Kitchen and bathroom hazards
steps: Keep birds away from hot pans, boiling water and open toilets.
Close bathroom doors and remove standing water hazards.
caution: Never leave a bird unsupervised near water or heat.

title: Warm weather care
steps: Provide shade, ventilation and plenty of fresh water.
Watch for panting, wings held away from the body and weakness.
caution: Heat stress is an emergency; contact an avian vet.

title: Cold weather care
steps: Keep the cage away from draughts and sudden temperature swings.
Maintain a stable indoor temperature and observe comfort.
caution: Avoid direct heaters and unsafe heat lamps.

title: Fireworks and loud noises
steps: Move the bird to a calm familiar room before noisy events.
Maintain a predictable routine and offer safe hiding options.
caution: Panic flights can cause injury; secure the enclosure.

title: Healthy sleep routines
steps: Provide a quiet, dark and predictable sleep period appropriate for the species.
Keep the cage away from late-night TV and disturbances.
caution: Ongoing sleep disruption can affect behaviour and health.

title: Signs of egg laying
steps: Watch for repeated nesting behaviour and changes in droppings or posture.
Discuss repeated laying and environmental management with an avian vet.
caution: Straining or sitting fluffed on the cage floor may indicate egg binding: urgent vet.

title: Avoiding accidental breeding
steps: Avoid nest boxes and enclosed nest-like spaces unless breeding is responsibly planned.
Ask an avian vet about hormone-related behaviours.
caution: Do not attempt to remove a retained egg yourself.

title: Caring for older birds
steps: Make food, water and favourite perches easy to reach.
Monitor weight, mobility and changes in routine.
caution: Arthritis or weakness needs veterinary assessment.

title: Recognising a frightened bird
steps: Watch for rapid breathing, retreating, freezing or repeated alarm calls.
Give space and reduce the stimulus rather than pursuing the bird.
caution: Forced handling can worsen fear and cause injury.

title: Preparing for holidays
steps: Arrange a knowledgeable bird sitter and written feeding and safety instructions.
Leave avian-vet details and emergency contact information.
caution: Do not leave a bird unattended for days with extra food alone.

title: Emergency contact card
steps: Record your avian vet, out-of-hours clinic and emergency contact.
Keep the bird's species, medicines and usual diet documented.
caution: Seek veterinary advice immediately for breathing problems, collapse or suspected poisoning.
